Here's the full pipeline for `fmt::format("{}", x)`, with the exact functions and files (this repo's fmt sources, under `include/fmt/` and `src/`):

## 1. Compile-time string check, then the public `format()` entry point

`"{}"` is passed as a `format_string<T...>` (a `fmt::detail::compile_string`-checked wrapper around `string_view`, defined in `include/fmt/base.h`), so the format string is validated against the argument types at compile time before anything runs.

The call lands in the variadic template at **`include/fmt/format.h:4362-4366`**:

```cpp
template <typename... T>
FMT_NODISCARD FMT_INLINE auto format(format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
    -> std::string {
  return vformat(fmt, fmt::make_format_args(args...));
}
```

Its whole job is to erase the argument-pack's types by calling `make_format_args`, then hand off to the non-template `vformat`.

## 2. Type-erasure: capturing arguments into `format_args`

`make_format_args` (**`include/fmt/base.h:2016`**) builds a `detail::format_arg_store<Context, NUM_ARGS, ...>` (**`base.h:1682`** / the no-named-args specialization at **`base.h:1716`**). Each argument is converted via `detail::make_arg` (**`base.h:1619-1661`**):

- `arg_mapper<Context>().map(val)` maps the concrete type down to one of fmt's small set of storable kinds (int, double, string_view, a generic pointer, or — for anything with a `formatter<T>` specialization — a `custom_value` holding a type-erased `format`/`parse` function pointer pair).
- The result is stored in `detail::value<Context>`, a union, wrapped either as a bare `value<Context>` (the "packed" fast path, ≤ `max_packed_args`) or a `basic_format_arg<Context>` (**`base.h:1726`**) which additionally carries a `detail::type` tag.

`format_arg_store` implicitly converts to `basic_format_args<Context>` (**`base.h:1842`**) — this is the type-erased container: for our single `"{}"`/`x` case it's packed, so `basic_format_args` just holds a type descriptor (`desc_`) and a pointer into the store's `value` array (`get(int id)` at **`base.h:1904`** reconstructs a `basic_format_arg` from that on demand). `format_args` is simply this template instantiated on the default `format_context`.

## 3. Routing through `vformat` → `vformat_to` into a memory buffer

`fmt::format`'s call resolves to the non-template, exported `FMT_API auto vformat(string_view fmt, format_args args) -> std::string` (declared **`format.h:4351`**, defined in **`include/fmt/format-inl.h:1431-1437`**):

```cpp
FMT_FUNC auto vformat(string_view fmt, format_args args) -> std::string {
  auto buffer = memory_buffer();
  detail::vformat_to(buffer, fmt, args);
  return to_string(buffer);
}
```

Being non-templated on `T...`, this is where fmt gets its compiled-library win: all the actual parsing/writing logic lives in one instantiation instead of being re-generated per call site.

- `memory_buffer` (**`format.h:936`**) is `basic_memory_buffer<char>` (**`format.h:835`**), a small-buffer-optimized, growable `detail::buffer<char>` (SSO array `store_`, doubling `grow()` at **`format.h:848-870`** that reallocates via `std::allocator` and `memcpy`s the old contents forward).
- `detail::vformat_to(buffer<Char>&, ..., args, locale_ref)` (**`format.h:4220-4286`**) does the real work. Notably it special-cases the exact `"{}"` format string (**`format.h:4223-4227`**):
  ```cpp
  if (fmt.size() == 2 && equal2(fmt.data(), "{}")) {
    auto arg = args.get(0);
    arg.visit(default_arg_formatter<Char>{out, args, loc});
    return;
  }
  ```
  For any other format string it drives `detail::parse_format_string` over a `format_handler` (**`format.h:4230-4284`**) whose callbacks (`on_text`, `on_replacement_field`, `on_format_specs`) parse literal text and `{...}` fields and dispatch each argument.

## 4. `formatter<T>` specializations write each argument

Dispatch happens through `basic_format_arg::visit` (**`base.h:1779-1800`**), a switch over the stored `detail::type` tag that calls a visitor with the concrete unwrapped value (or, for user-defined types, a `handle` wrapping the type-erased `custom_value`).

- For built-in/fundamental types, the visitor is `default_arg_formatter`/`arg_formatter` (**`format.h:3718-3754`**), whose `operator()(T value)` calls `detail::write<Char>(out, value[, specs, locale])` — fmt's internal fast integer/float/string formatting routines that append characters straight to the buffer via the `basic_appender<Char>` output iterator (**`base.h:1154`**, wraps `detail::buffer<T>::append`).
- For a user-defined type `x` with a `formatter<T>` specialization (**`base.h:1140-1144`**, the primary template that must be specialized, e.g. via `formatter<T> : formatter<string_view>` or similar), the `handle::format` overload (**`base.h:1751-1754`**) or the generic `write<>` overload at **`format.h:3702-3714`** instantiates `Context::formatter_type<T>`, calls its `parse(parse_ctx)` on any format spec, then its `format(value, ctx)`, which is expected to write through `ctx.out()` (again a `basic_appender` into the same buffer). This is the customization point that lets any type plug into `{}`.

## 5. Turning the buffer back into a `std::string`

Once `vformat_to` returns, control is back in `detail::vformat` (step 2 above), which calls `to_string(buffer)` (**`format.h:4201-4207`**):

```cpp
template <typename Char, size_t SIZE>
FMT_NODISCARD auto to_string(const basic_memory_buffer<Char, SIZE>& buf)
    -> std::basic_string<Char> {
  auto size = buf.size();
  return std::basic_string<Char>(buf.data(), size);
}
```

This does one final copy from the (possibly heap-grown) `memory_buffer`'s contiguous storage into a freshly constructed `std::string`, which is what `fmt::format` returns to the caller.

```
fmt::format("{}", x)                         (format.h:4363)

 └─ fmt::vformat(fmt, args)                  (format-inl.h:1431)
     ├─ memory_buffer buffer;                (format.h:835/936)
     ├─ detail::vformat_to(buffer, fmt, args)(format.h:4220)
```
